program A · the sovereignty core

The harness exit — pydantic-ai, honestly

58 modules under spruce_grove/ import pydantic-ai directly (76 reference it). It owns the agent loop, streaming, tool calling, model resolution, and the retry/refresh seams. A big-bang removal is a rewrite masquerading as a cleanup — so the exit is a staged seam, one call site per landing, tests green each time. Source of truth: SOVEREIGNTY.md.

stagewhat happensstatus
1 · Inventory & freezeevery touchpoint mapped: pydantic_patches, model_factory, base_agent, event_stream_handler, round_robin_model, CLI bootstrap, MCP bridgesdone
2 · The seamspruce_grove/harness/ live: grove-owned Harness protocol (zero external imports, structurally tested), delegating adapter (parity proven), soft-failing selector (SPRUCE_GROVE_HARNESS). First two call sites migrated: subagent_invocation, private_inference.landed 2026-09-15
3 · Call-site migrations56 files remain, in order: settings surface (load_config/make_model_settings) → the RunContext tool vocabulary (the ~40-module long tail) → the agent loop + streaming. One landing at a time, parity tests each.next landing queued
4 · The replacementthe grove's own loop behind the protocol: stdlib + httpx streaming, the tolerant OpenAI client we already carry, our own retry/token logic (http_retry.py, claude_oauth_transport.py, tolerant_openai.py exist as seeds). Gate: tried & true in production before the flag flips — the seam runs both side by side.queued · seeds exist
5 · The flip & the pruneflip per-model/per-agent behind config, then delete. Ends with pydantic-ai gone from pyproject and PROVENANCE.md updated.awaits 3–4

Honesty note: the boot banner no longer advertises the framework (that was branding); the dependency itself is still real and still counts itself honestly here.

program C · governance

The council & the wall — what's waiting on the founder

Three stewards, 2/3 and 3/3 thresholds, an emergency lane, and a rule for public pages: never persons, never companies — only the ethos. The wall is not armed yet; branch protection on main is still off (by choice, until the stewards exist to enforce it with).

Full census in docs/DEPENDENCY-EXIT.md (six tiers, verdicts computed by import scans). The ladder in execution order — a rung flips to done only with its receipt: tests green, hash proof, or a diff.

Already computed and documented: httpx2 is load-bearing (codex/claude transports), termflow-md renders tool output, ripgrep powers the grep tool, agent-client-protocol backs the ACP agent surface, Docker images are the exit rails (pin digests at stand-up). npm/axios: absent everywhere.

The validation ladder — what proves the grove next

Spec written 2026-09-16 in docs/VALIDATION-LADDER.md. These are the product-shaped proofs that turn a tool into a home.

validationwhat it meansfoundation already landedstatus
Desktop OS onboardingpersona-driven first run that configures agents, plugins, voice, telemetry, and model tier to the user's use case; the download → subscription → first successful run path in under five minutes; token economy and context utilization tuned from minute oneonboarding wizard skeleton, /add_model, keyring credentials, cohort plugins, desktop shell v0.1.0 (Tauri, separate repo)design · ladder: persona survey → tuned defaults → subscription flow → time-to-first-success metric
Traceability programmatrices mapping every feature, button, command, flag, and history-view behavior to the test that proves it, the build-log entry that birthed it, and the observatory narrative that explains it — generated from the registries, never hand-kept7,873-test suite, pexpect TUI harness, build-log 32 entries, observatory pipelinedesign · computed-from-registries approach agreed
The living directoryopening a folder loads it as an organism: pulses (what's hot, what changed), hooks (discovered extension points), telemetry + audit (what happened, how, why — observatory treatment), all voice-driven via mockingbird; the view small-business users will live inbrowser tool suite, observability module, audit logging, mockingbird plugin, /rec voice loopdesign · concept captured
program F · the proof grounds

The wedges — where the grove meets real users

The grove's thesis is that voice-first agentic tools should serve the people the industry forgot: the trades, the small gyms, the family. These programs are run from a private, local-only lab — the public repo carries the product ideas, never the people or the businesses.

wedgestatenext
Small-business portfoliotwo local-business studies complete using the proven playbook (brand, mission, ownership, franchising constraints, systems audit, digital presence, opportunity notes). Findings: one books jobs by mailto: with zero online booking; one runs a commercial gym portal with no public schedule and an expansion coming — both are exactly the gap the grove's small-business kit fills.pick one → depth interview → systems audit → proposal
Family labvoice-first computing for the smallest builders: a wiped-and-optimized Linux rig, a kid-safe voice loop, a school-communications portal that turns newsletters and portals into a weekly digest, and extracurricular micro-projects. Planned locally; private by design.rig build this week · portal scaffold next
Cohort pluginsJunto, barber, backoffice, creative scaffold — the persona-shaped plugin seeds are versioned in-repo (user-plugins/)shipped · grows with each wedge
how we got here

The trail so far — computed from the commit log

Thirteen days from fork to this page. Every date below is a real commit date.

2026-09-03

The fork

First commit: Code Puppy imported from upstream (Michael Pfaffenberger's MIT project), synced and renamed — the seedling transplanted into the grove.

2026-09-11

v1.0.1 goes public

First PyPI release. The voice-first wedge is already the reason the fork exists.

2026-09-15 · morning

The great relicense & the rebrand

MIT → Apache-2.0 with the upstream notice preserved verbatim; logos/ brand kit (Core Disc, Grove Marks, Ghost, Lockups); sprucegrove.io relaunched per-audience; the bootloader speaks only grove.

2026-09-15 · midday

The self-healing loop + the harness seam

Auto-update closes the loop from version check to actuation. The sovereignty seam lands: grove-owned Harness protocol, delegating adapter, soft-failing selector — first two call sites migrated.

2026-09-15 · evening

Governance, observatory, the board

Council + approval wall + compat-exit ledger; the release observatory with provenance chips; the execution board + automation kit (wall, backups, parity, Forgejo stack); session handoff written; the dashboard and dependency census go public.

2026-09-16 · today

The validation ladder + the wedges

Three validations spec'd (desktop onboarding, traceability, living directory); two business studies complete; the release-notes pipeline automated; this page.

adopted · parked on purpose

The north star — grove on metal

When the core is grove-owned end to end and stdlib-lean, the long-horizon track opens: a runtime small enough to wake on real hardware, agnostic across Linux/macOS/Windows first, bare-metal eventually (tracked on the board, bead 5al.7). It is the destination, not the next step — and it inherits every gate and every test the seam lands along the way. Privacy-first telemetry (the r2j bead) rides the same ladder.

“The harness is borrowed. The grove is ours.
Leave it better than we found it.”
together we are better, always
